description: A Muse Code login's quota: the new core's GET /v0/management/accounts/{id}/quota against the key-endpoint request today's panel sends through the old core's api-call relay.

headers.Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, X-Api-Key, X-Goog-Api-Key, Anthropic-Version, Anthropic-Beta
headers.Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
headers.Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-CPA-TRACE-ID, X-CPA-VERSION, X-CPA-COMMIT, X-CPA-BUILD-DATE, X-CPA-SUPPORT-PLUGIN, X-CPA-HOME-VERSION, X-CPA-HOME-BUILD-DATE, X-SERVER-VERSION, X-SERVER-BUILD-DATE, Location, Retry-After, ETag, X-Request-Id, OpenAI-Request-Id

exceptions.reason: Different management API by design: the old core's api-call relay answers with the upstream's reply wrapped as {status_code, header, body} for the panel to read, and the panel works out the plan and limits itself; the new core's quota call reads the account's quota itself and answers {quota, fetched_at}. The want pins the new quota for this upstream reply.
Different management API by design: the new management API answers application/json; today's core's gin handlers add a charset.

Quota fetchers use each provider's own client identity for its own subscription (a decision on record): the new core sends Muse Code's own User-Agent; the panel's request sets none, so the relay sends Go's default.
The new core sends Muse Code's client identity headers on the key-endpoint call (README: Meta, Quota); the panel's request sends only Accept, Content-Type, Authorization and x-api-version.
